column1: # WPT area refusals: area<TAB>ADR/reason
# Each line maps a WPT area (as it appears in directories.txt and wpt-baseline.md)
# to the ADR that says this browser will not implement the capability it tests.
# Only areas in our directories.txt checkout are listed here. Areas not checked
# out (webrtc/, geolocation/, webaudio/, etc.) are implicitly refused by their
# absence from directories.txt.
# A refusal means: do not chase this area's pass rate. A test we refuse is a
# decision with a name, not a bug. The ceiling table marks these as "refused".
# Partial refusals (area has some refused and some implemented tests) are noted
# but the area is NOT marked refused -- its ceiling is Firefox's rate on the
# tests this browser can run.
# --- Full refusals: the entire area is out of scope ---
# (none of the checked-out areas are fully refused; areas like webrtc/ and
# geolocation/ are not in directories.txt at all)
# --- Partial refusals: some tests in the area are blocked by ADR decisions ---
# These are NOT marked as refused in the ceiling table. They are documented here
# so an agent working the area knows which failures are deliberate.
# html/: ADR 0011/0012/0026 -- document.write deliberately unimplemented
# html/browsers/: ADR 0026 §6 -- window.open returns null, opener absent
# workers/: ADR 0022 §1 -- SharedWorker refused (DedicatedWorker implemented)
# content-security-policy/: ADR 0020 §3 -- report-uri/report-to/Report-Only not implemented
# css/selectors/: ADR 0012/0016/0033 -- :visited matches nothing (privacy)
# streams/: ADR 0020 §1 -- new ReadableStream({start}) illegal constructor
# IndexedDB/: ADR 0021/0038 -- memory tier only, no disk persistence by default
# websockets/: server does not speak WebSocket protocol (infrastructure, not ADR refusal)
# domparsing/: DOMParser absent (returns second Document, session-log deliberate absence)
